LEVELS.name: Beginner
LEVELS.idea: Use AI on small, real tasks and check what it gives you.

LEVELS.name: Experienced
LEVELS.idea: Give it your context, standards and limits, and choose how to work per task.

LEVELS.name: Leading
LEVELS.idea: Change how you work and what you take on, and lift the people around you.

SCOPES.name: Yourself
SCOPES.lede: How you work on your own.

SCOPES.name: Your team
SCOPES.lede: What you take initiative on, so the team uses AI well and keeps quality.

SCOPES.name: The client
SCOPES.lede: What you advise and push for in the client's organization.

team: Agree which tools and rules the team uses, and that no agent writes to production.
Put shared skills, decision records and review rules where every person and agent reads them.
Rework the team's process for agents, and agree who owns what.
org: Find out which tools and data the client allows, and help them write it down if nobody has.
Help the client connect agents to their documentation and knowledge base, read-only.
Help the client build one agreed way of working with agents, and name who owns it.

self: Use an assistant on one small, real task every day, and check the result.
Turn one routine you repeat every week into a skill.
Decide what is worth doing this week, and run agents on the rest.
tests: You have used AI on real work five days in a row, and you can explain everything you delivered
A colleague would get the same quality with your setup
Work gets done while you do something else, and others use what you built

self: Install a coding agent in a repository you know, and let it make one small change you read line by line.
Put conventions, decision records and tests in the repository, so a fresh session follows them.
Run several sessions with one checking another, and test the architecture itself.
tests: You have merged an agent-written change that you fully understand
A fresh agent session follows your conventions without being told
You steer several agents and still know why the code looks the way it does

self: Transcribe one interview, ask for patterns, and check them against your own notes.
Deliver one design change as a pull request.
Start your day from pull requests, and share your research setup with the team.
tests: You have checked an AI summary against your raw material
You have delivered a design change as a pull request
You can review a design change that arrives as code, and a colleague uses your setup

self: Describe a real problem to the assistant, and let it ask you questions before it answers.
Keep meetings and sources in one knowledge base the assistant can read.
Automate the low-value tasks, so you get more time with clients and consultants.
tests: You describe problems to it instead of only asking for facts
A new deliverable starts from your knowledge base, not a blank page
Something useful is prepared for you every week without you asking

self: Set up a project for one client or case, and transcribe one meeting into it.
Ask your interview material how people reasoned, not only what they said.
Build checks into your process that catch errors before the client does.
tests: An AI-assisted draft has gone out in your name after your own checks
You can ask your material how people reasoned, and check the answer
Your process catches a wrong figure before the client does

TOPICS.what: Start small, and challenge the answers
TOPICS.detail: Use it on small, real tasks from today's work. Disagree with it when you know better. Nobody is behind.
TOPICS.why: You learn what it is good at without risking real work. Your expertise is what catches its mistakes.
TOPICS.ask: When did you last disagree with the agent and turn out to be right?

how.text: DataCamp, if you like a course to follow

TOPICS.what: Models and the app around them
TOPICS.detail: The model is not the app. Model families differ in strengths, input types and price.
TOPICS.why: You judge all AI by one tool's weak spots, and expect the wrong things.
TOPICS.ask: Can you name a task where another model or app does better than your default?

TOPICS.what: Token management: cost, quality and climate
TOPICS.detail: Tokens, effort, context size and model choice decide what a task costs and how good it gets. The strongest model at full effort is not the default.
TOPICS.why: Throwing frontier models at everything can be lose-lose: worse results, a large bill for the client, poor return and more energy used.
TOPICS.ask: Do you know roughly what your last task cost, and whether a smaller model would have done?

TOPICS.what: Prompt at the right level
TOPICS.detail: Be concrete about the goal, the limits and the size of the task. Be open about the solution, and let the agent propose. Do not polish the wording.
TOPICS.why: Dictating the solution gives you the wrong thing. A vague goal gives you vague work.
TOPICS.ask: When did you last ask for options instead of dictating the answer?

TOPICS.what: Grilling: let the agent interview you first
TOPICS.detail: Before it makes anything, the agent asks you questions until you agree on what to make.
TOPICS.why: You and the agent agree on the goal before work starts, and it finds gaps you would miss.
TOPICS.ask: Has an agent asked you ten questions before producing anything?

TOPICS.what: Plan first, and keep research apart from doing
TOPICS.why: You make the important choices yourself, and keep your own competence.
TOPICS.ask: Do you read and correct a plan before the agent acts?

TOPICS.what: Context, and when to start a new session
TOPICS.detail: Know what the agent sees, when a session has gone stale, and how to hand over to a fresh one.
TOPICS.why: Answers get worse in long sessions, and tokens burn.
TOPICS.ask: Do you know when a session has gone stale?

TOPICS.what: Use it to explain and to think with
TOPICS.detail: Describe the problem and ask why, not only for facts or fixes.
TOPICS.why: It is not a better search engine. It helps you reason.
TOPICS.ask: Do you describe problems to it, or only ask for answers?

TOPICS.what: Keep sensitive data out
TOPICS.detail: Know which data the client allows in which tool. Mask sensitive data on the way in.
TOPICS.why: A privacy breach at the client.
TOPICS.ask: Do you know the data rule for your current client?

TOPICS.what: Connect the sources you work in, and decide what not to connect
TOPICS.why: Without them you copy and paste. Connect too much and private conversations leak.
TOPICS.ask: Can you list what your assistant can read right now?

TOPICS.what: Use ready-made skills
TOPICS.detail: A skill is a packaged instruction the agent loads for a kind of task. Start with skills others wrote.
TOPICS.why: You get good routines without writing them yourself.
TOPICS.ask: Have you installed a skill and used it on real work?

TOPICS.what: You own what you deliver
TOPICS.why: Work can look fine without being in place.
TOPICS.ask: Could you explain every part of your last delivery without the agent?

TOPICS.what: A coding agent with plan mode, and an inline assistant in the IDE
TOPICS.why: In a chat window you copy and paste, and the agent never sees the codebase.
TOPICS.ask: Has an agent made a change across several files for you?

TOPICS.what: Give the agent a clear goal, by one of two routes
TOPICS.detail: Write an issue or spec the agent can solve from the text alone. Or build your own mental model and leave TODOs in the code for the agent.
TOPICS.why: The agent writes the code, so our job is to set better goals.
TOPICS.ask: Could an agent solve your last issue from the text alone?

how.text: Matt Pocock's skills for writing issues

TOPICS.what: Use the agent to explain code and odd behavior
TOPICS.why: You miss the cheapest way to learn a codebase.
TOPICS.ask: Do you ask why before you ask for a fix?

TOPICS.what: Solid software engineering fundamentals
TOPICS.why: You cannot judge what the agent hands you.
TOPICS.ask: Which part of the agent's last change would you have done differently?

TOPICS.what: Split work into small tasks
TOPICS.detail: This matters more than ever. A pull request should be a gift.
TOPICS.why: Large changes nobody can review.
TOPICS.ask: Would you enjoy reviewing your last pull request?

TOPICS.what: An AGENTS.md in the repository, and handover between sessions
TOPICS.why: Each session starts cold, or drags stale context along.
TOPICS.ask: What does a new session know about your repository before you type?

TOPICS.what: Try different coding agents and models
TOPICS.why: You settle on the first setup that worked.
TOPICS.ask: Have you given the same task to two tools?

TOPICS.what: Give the design agent your Figma structure, not a screenshot
TOPICS.why: A sketched screen gives the agent very little.
TOPICS.ask: Does the agent get your components, or only a picture?

TOPICS.what: Git and GitHub: clone, branch, pull request
TOPICS.why: You cannot deliver design as code, or follow work that lives in repositories.
TOPICS.ask: Can you open a pull request and read someone else's?

TOPICS.what: AI in every research step
TOPICS.detail: Research questions, interviews, transcripts, summaries, common patterns and ideas.
TOPICS.why: You run the old process at the old speed.
TOPICS.ask: Which research step has not changed yet?

TOPICS.what: Transcribe meetings and interviews
TOPICS.detail: For example the transcription in Word, Trale or Jamie. Ask for consent first.
TOPICS.why: Analysis starts from memory and scattered notes, and details get lost.
TOPICS.ask: Is your last important meeting searchable?

TOPICS.what: Structure research data so it can be found
TOPICS.why: The agent cannot answer from material it cannot find.
TOPICS.ask: Could the agent find every interview on one theme?

TOPICS.what: Critical analysis at each handoff
TOPICS.why: Confident summaries with errors reach the client.
TOPICS.ask: Do you check the synthesis against the raw material?

TOPICS.what: The assistant as a sparring partner
TOPICS.why: You use it as a search engine and miss what it is good at.
TOPICS.ask: Do you describe problems to it, or only ask for facts?

TOPICS.what: Connect email, statistics and the systems you work in
TOPICS.why: The agent only knows what you paste in.
TOPICS.ask: Which daily system is still not connected?

TOPICS.what: Know what MCP, skills and Git are
TOPICS.why: You cannot follow where the tools are going, or talk about them with clients.
TOPICS.ask: Can you explain what a skill is to a colleague?

TOPICS.what: A project per client or case, as a sparring partner
TOPICS.why: Every conversation starts from zero, and the material is spread out.
TOPICS.ask: Does the assistant know the case before you start typing?

TOPICS.what: Connect files, spreadsheets and Office 365, and decide what to leave out
TOPICS.why: It is easy to lose control of a spreadsheet, and private conversations should not be connected.
TOPICS.ask: Which of your connected sources holds something private?

TOPICS.what: Build trust by checking output against the source
TOPICS.why: Too much trust or none at all. Both cost you.
TOPICS.ask: How do you check a number the agent gives you?

TOPICS.what: Tone of voice
TOPICS.why: Text that does not sound like you.
TOPICS.ask: Would a client recognize your voice in the draft?

TOPICS.what: Agree what the team uses
TOPICS.detail: Tools, skills and one set of instructions every agent reads.
TOPICS.why: Everyone uses agents their own way, and quality depends on who did the task.
TOPICS.ask: Is there one file that tells every agent how the team works?

TOPICS.what: No agent writes to production
TOPICS.why: One mistake becomes an incident.
TOPICS.ask: Can any agent on the team reach production today?

TOPICS.what: Roles, boundaries and definition of done
TOPICS.why: Nobody knows when a part is finished, or who owns it.
TOPICS.ask: Who owns a change a designer delivers as code?

TOPICS.what: Share what works
TOPICS.detail: A channel and a regular slot for what people learn about AI.
TOPICS.why: Everyone rediscovers the same things.
TOPICS.ask: When did the team last share an AI finding?

TOPICS.what: Help the client publish which tools and plugins are allowed
TOPICS.why: People avoid the tools, or install anything.
TOPICS.ask: Can someone at the client find out what is allowed in a minute?

TOPICS.what: Help the client set rules for which data can go where
TOPICS.why: Confidentiality rests on individual guesses.
TOPICS.ask: Does everyone at the client know the rule for their own data?

TOPICS.what: Help the client set up a shared way to learn
TOPICS.detail: A planned path and a sharing culture, not chance.
TOPICS.why: Learning is mostly random.
TOPICS.ask: Is there a planned path at the client, or do people find things by chance?

TOPICS.what: Choose how to work, based on the task
TOPICS.detail: Pick how much to hand over based on the context, how correct the result must be, and how much you need a correct mental model of the system. A developer picks between a spec, TODOs in code, or a one-shot. A designer between a throwaway exploration and a deliverable. A business role between a draft for yourself and a figure for the client.
TOPICS.why: One way of working for everything is either too slow or too risky.
TOPICS.ask: On your last task, did you choose how much to hand over, or do what you always do?

TOPICS.what: Pick model and effort per job
TOPICS.detail: For example a strong model to plan and orchestrate, and a cheaper one to implement.
TOPICS.why: Slow and expensive runs, or weak plans.
TOPICS.ask: Do you know which model and effort did your last task?

TOPICS.what: Write your own skills, and know which to keep personal
TOPICS.why: You repeat the same instructions, and the quality varies.
TOPICS.ask: Have you written a skill for something you do every week?

TOPICS.what: Connect project context through MCP, read-only by default
TOPICS.detail: The backlog, docs, logs and dashboards. For example the Atlassian plugin or a Grafana MCP.
TOPICS.why: The agent guesses about things it could look up.
TOPICS.ask: Which system would save you most time if the agent could read it?

TOPICS.what: Use your craft and domain knowledge to steer
TOPICS.why: Generic output, and no way to tell good from bad.
TOPICS.ask: Where did your expertise change the result last week?

TOPICS.what: A fixed way to review agent output at every handoff
TOPICS.why: Errors pass on to the client or the next person.
TOPICS.ask: Do you have a fixed way of checking agent output?

TOPICS.what: Permissions and sandboxing
TOPICS.detail: Know what an agent on your machine may read and change. Developers can run agents in a sandbox, for example Docker.
TOPICS.why: An agent with your full access makes your worst mistake at machine speed.
TOPICS.ask: What is the most damaging thing your agent could do today?

TOPICS.what: Use AI to learn, not only to fetch information
TOPICS.why: You get faster but not better.
TOPICS.ask: Have you asked the agent to teach you something this month?

TOPICS.what: A healthy codebase with conventions and good examples
TOPICS.why: Agents copy the patterns they find, bad ones too.
TOPICS.ask: Would a new session find one clear way to do things?

TOPICS.what: Less time on prompts, more on domain and architecture tests
TOPICS.why: Nothing stops the agent from drifting.
TOPICS.ask: Do your tests check the domain, or only utilities?

TOPICS.what: Build your own mental model before the change
TOPICS.why: Review gets harder than writing would have been.
TOPICS.ask: Can you sketch the change before the agent makes it?

TOPICS.what: Grilling with docs, decision records and time on the domain
TOPICS.why: Decisions vanish, and each session starts from zero.
TOPICS.ask: Where are your last three design decisions written down?

TOPICS.what: Application and system architecture
TOPICS.why: The agent does not know which direction to go. Developers still know best.
TOPICS.ask: Who decided the structure of your last feature?

TOPICS.what: Mix manual review with AI review
TOPICS.why: Review becomes a bottleneck or a rubber stamp.
TOPICS.ask: How much of your week is review now?

TOPICS.what: Several sessions with a clear overview
TOPICS.detail: For example tmux or remote sessions.
TOPICS.why: It is easy to lose control.
TOPICS.ask: Can you say what each of your running sessions is doing right now?

TOPICS.what: Reverse engineering, prototyping and infrastructure as code with AI
TOPICS.why: You only use agents for feature work.
TOPICS.ask: Have you used an agent on infrastructure or legacy code?

TOPICS.what: Design to code: where the handover reinterprets
TOPICS.why: The built result drifts from the design.
TOPICS.ask: Do you know where your design gets reinterpreted?

TOPICS.what: Explore instead of imagine
TOPICS.detail: Try other clicks, other scales and other domains, instead of thinking them through.
TOPICS.why: UX flows thought through for one case only.
TOPICS.ask: How many variants did you test before choosing?

TOPICS.what: Know what is worth making, tied to the product strategy
TOPICS.why: Cheap production leads to low-value work.
TOPICS.ask: Can you tie your last prototype to a product goal?

TOPICS.what: How an agent loop works, when you design agent products
TOPICS.why: You design for a system you do not understand.
TOPICS.ask: Can you describe the loop behind your product?

TOPICS.what: Research analysis by meaning, not only by words
TOPICS.detail: Ask your interview material how people talked about and reasoned around a topic. Still do the interviews yourself.
TOPICS.why: Analysis stays at four to five hours per interview hour.
TOPICS.ask: Can you ask your material how people reasoned?

TOPICS.what: A second brain: meetings and sources in one knowledge base
TOPICS.why: Information cannot be combined for decisions.
TOPICS.ask: Where would the agent find what you learned last quarter?

how.text: Andrej Karpathy on personal knowledge bases

TOPICS.what: Structured input, many outputs
TOPICS.detail: Reports, templates and business cases from the same material.
TOPICS.why: Each deliverable is handmade from zero.
TOPICS.ask: Has the agent filled your standard template from raw data?

TOPICS.what: Scheduled tasks that prepare work before you need it
TOPICS.why: You prepare every meeting by hand.
TOPICS.ask: What gets prepared for you automatically each week?

TOPICS.what: Voice recordings as input
TOPICS.why: You lose thoughts away from the keyboard.
TOPICS.ask: Do you talk your notes in?

TOPICS.what: Git basics, for knowledge bases and skills kept as files
TOPICS.why: You cannot share or version what you build.
TOPICS.ask: Could a colleague get your skills and notes without you emailing them?

TOPICS.what: AI and ethics, and AI for business leaders
TOPICS.why: You advise on something you have not studied.
TOPICS.ask: Have you taken a structured course?

TOPICS.what: Connect the assistant to Figma and workshop tools
TOPICS.why: You move things between tools by hand.
TOPICS.ask: Has an agent built a workshop board for you?

TOPICS.what: Use your experience to create, not to skip experience
TOPICS.why: Polished output with nothing behind it.
TOPICS.ask: What in your last deliverable could only you have added?

TOPICS.what: Shared, project-specific skills
TOPICS.detail: In the repository or a shared space. For example skills for your stack and for handling secrets.
TOPICS.why: Agents get your stack wrong the same way every time.
TOPICS.ask: Does everyone run the same skills for planning and review?

TOPICS.what: Decision records, post mortems and runbooks
TOPICS.detail: Readable by people, numbered and dated, kept where the agent can read them.
TOPICS.why: Decisions vanish, and the agent cannot act on knowledge that lives in people's heads.
TOPICS.ask: Could an agent follow your runbook for the last incident?

TOPICS.what: Shared rules for review, and one shared first review by an agent
TOPICS.why: Review quality depends on who reviews.
TOPICS.ask: Does every pull request get the same first review?

TOPICS.what: Guardrails set up once for everyone
TOPICS.detail: Sandboxing, read-only by default, and secrets handled through skills.
TOPICS.why: Each agent can reach everything its owner can.
TOPICS.ask: Is sandboxing set up once, or left to each person?

TOPICS.what: Pair through prompting on hard problems
TOPICS.why: Decisions made by one person and one agent.
TOPICS.ask: Have two of you prompted together on a hard problem?

TOPICS.what: Written practices, shared mental models, and follow-up on how each person works
TOPICS.why: Juniors dump the task into the agent and push it, without seeing the bigger picture.
TOPICS.ask: Do you know how each person on the team works with agents?

how.text: pstack, a set of skills for a full development flow

TOPICS.what: Connect documentation and knowledge bases, also for development
TOPICS.why: Agents cannot look up base data and domain information.
TOPICS.ask: Can a coding agent at the client look up domain facts without someone pasting them in?

TOPICS.what: A shared knowledge base
TOPICS.why: Information is spread over many systems and cannot support decisions.
TOPICS.ask: Could an agent answer a question about a past project at the client?

TOPICS.what: Local models where privacy requires it
TOPICS.why: Some clients cannot use cloud AI at all.
TOPICS.ask: What do you advise a client that forbids cloud models?

TOPICS.what: Make time for quality culture
TOPICS.why: Culture loses to delivery every week.
TOPICS.ask: Is time for this in anyone's plan at the client?

TOPICS.what: Take a broader product role
TOPICS.detail: Change how you work, what you take responsibility for and which positions you take. You are still a technical expert, but above all an expert in turning the real world into systems, processes and formal structures that work as modelled.
TOPICS.why: Making things gets cheap, so judgment about what to make and why is what counts. Caring about what you make matters even more.
TOPICS.ask: What did you take responsibility for this month that is outside your title?

how.text: Laurie Voss's talk on becoming product engineers

TOPICS.what: Choose what you should do, not what you can do
TOPICS.why: A pile of nice-to-haves nobody asked for.
TOPICS.ask: What did you decide not to make this week?

TOPICS.what: Several agents at once
TOPICS.detail: Subagents, parallel sessions and orchestration, with one agent checking another.
TOPICS.why: You wait on one agent, or run many and lose quality.
TOPICS.ask: Does anything other than you check the agent's work?

TOPICS.what: Manage cognitive load and text fatigue
TOPICS.why: You stop reading what the agents write.
TOPICS.ask: How much agent output did you skim this week?

TOPICS.what: Build processes and systems, not single outputs
TOPICS.detail: For example onboarding, or a research setup others can run.
TOPICS.why: The gain stays with one task and one person.
TOPICS.ask: Which of your routines could a colleague run tomorrow?

TOPICS.what: Curate your skills
TOPICS.detail: Prune and rewrite them, know when no skill is needed, and share the good ones with the team and the client.
TOPICS.why: Skills pile up and fill the context.
TOPICS.ask: Which skill did you last delete or rewrite?

TOPICS.what: Assess the risks of connected tools
TOPICS.why: Security comes second to hype.
TOPICS.ask: Do you know what an MCP server you installed can do?

TOPICS.what: Tests for the application architecture itself
TOPICS.why: Structure erodes one merge at a time.
TOPICS.ask: Would a test fail if an agent broke your layering?

TOPICS.what: Agentic on-call and triage across agents
TOPICS.why: Operations stays manual while development speeds up.
TOPICS.ask: Could an agent do the first ten minutes of your last incident?

TOPICS.what: Your own agent setup and local models
TOPICS.why: You depend on defaults you do not understand, and some data stays off limits.
TOPICS.ask: Do you know what a local model can and cannot do for you?

TOPICS.what: How MCP works inside
TOPICS.why: You install servers you cannot assess.
TOPICS.ask: Have you read the code of an MCP server you use?

TOPICS.what: Routing skills that load others only when needed
TOPICS.why: Context fills up and quality drops.
TOPICS.ask: Do your skills load only when the task needs them?

TOPICS.what: A workday that starts from pull requests
TOPICS.why: You become the bottleneck when others send code.
TOPICS.ask: Can you review a design change that arrives as code?

TOPICS.what: Read design out of code with the agent's help
TOPICS.why: Changes land that no designer has seen.
TOPICS.ask: How do you look at a pull request you cannot read?

TOPICS.what: Write down the new practices for the field
TOPICS.why: Everyone invents their own method, and the skill stays with one person.
TOPICS.ask: Has your team written down how you research with AI?

TOPICS.what: Automate the tasks that take time but do not matter
TOPICS.why: Less face time with clients and consultants.
TOPICS.ask: What took an hour last week that an agent could have done?

TOPICS.what: Skills for business routines
TOPICS.why: You know of skills but have not seen the value, so it stays untried.
TOPICS.ask: Have you tried one skill on a real task?

TOPICS.what: Protect quality and correctness in the whole system
TOPICS.why: Errors multiply when automation scales.
TOPICS.ask: What catches a wrong figure before the client does?

TOPICS.what: AI in forecasting work
TOPICS.why: Forecasts stay manual.
TOPICS.ask: Which part of your forecast could an agent prepare?

TOPICS.what: New ways of working as teams get smaller
TOPICS.why: A process built for more people.
TOPICS.ask: What would you stop doing with three people?

TOPICS.what: Ownership shared by people and agents
TOPICS.why: Shared ownership of the code gets lost.
TOPICS.ask: Who on your team knows why the code looks the way it does?

TOPICS.what: Test the codebase and conventions, not only the application
TOPICS.why: Agents break conventions nothing protects.
TOPICS.ask: Which team convention is enforced by a test?

TOPICS.what: One agreed way of building with agents
TOPICS.detail: A software factory, built into existing workflows, with a named owner. It takes large, systematic change.
TOPICS.why: AI use stays a personal habit.
TOPICS.ask: Can the client describe their way of building with agents in one sentence?

TOPICS.what: Make someone own the question of what to do differently
TOPICS.detail: Beyond solving each day's tasks.
TOPICS.why: Tasks get optimized, and the purpose gets missed.
TOPICS.ask: Who at the client is responsible for that question?

TOPICS.what: Build AI into the systems where work happens
TOPICS.detail: For example an assistant connected to the CV system.
TOPICS.why: AI stays a side window.
TOPICS.ask: Which client system should have this built in first?
